title: 📰 AI news · November 20

items.title: Meta's AI agent peeked into Signal
items.text: Reuters tested Meta's Muse agent: on Android it read Signal messages through the notification access granted at first setup. If you run a bot or an agent on AI, it works with the permissions you gave it too. Check which accesses you gave your agent during setup.

items.title: Transport for London breach: 265,000 people
items.text: Names, phones, emails, addresses, birth dates and security questions with answers leaked for Oyster photocard holders. If you use the same answers elsewhere, they can be guessed. Change security answers wherever they repeat.

items.title: Edge is testing a Lockdown mode
items.text: The mode turns off WebGL and WebGPU, the ways websites use your graphics card, so the browser is harder to break out of its sandbox. It is in the Canary build, and sites with games and maps may behave differently.

items.title: Gemini works on your Mac
items.text: The agent in the Gemini Mac app opens programs, fills in forms, sorts files and builds slides. You can approve each step. For now it is in English in the US, with a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra plan.

items.title: Anthropic raised $81.3 billion
items.text: 980 million shares sold at $83. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC bought another $26 billion. TechCrunch sees it as a test of AI's circular financing.

items.title: Intel found its first outside customer for 18A chips
items.text: CEO Lip-Bu Tan said yields on 18A reached 70%. Intel shares rose 8%.

takeaway: Today's stories are about access: agents and services work with what they were allowed at setup. Recommendation: open your agent's settings and remove accesses it does not need.
